title: The Unquiet Letter
premise: Retired detective Felix Kavanagh has quietly solved three deaths the police ruled accidental, but when a drowned woman washes up wearing clothes stolen from the closet of Maren Voss — the key witness in his last case, officially dead for six years — he realizes someone is staging her death over and over to keep it believed. Following a letter Maren mailed him the week she vanished, Felix uncovers a coastal land-development conspiracy that murdered witnesses and bought its respectability with the town's grief. The trail ends at the flooded quarry where Maren faked her drowning and has been hiding in plain sight as the town's reclusive archivist; to expose the conspiracy without destroying her, Felix must let the tide give up what it took — the conspirators' own buried evidence — and choose between justice and mercy.
about_author: Yara Ishikawa is a former maritime archivist who spent a decade cataloguing shipwreck records along the northern coast before turning to fiction. She writes mysteries about towns that remember more than they admit.

chapters.title: Salt on the Threshold
chapters.summary: Felix Kavanagh opens his failing bookshop on a gray morning and finds a police card on the mat: another 'accidental' death by water. In flashback we learn of the three deaths he quietly solved. POV: Felix. Beat: weary competence masking loneliness.

chapters.title: The Wrong Clothes
chapters.summary: The drowned woman is identified as a drifter, but Felix recognizes the dress: it belonged to Maren Voss, the witness declared dead six years ago whose testimony once ruined him professionally. POV: Felix. Beat: cold shock — the past has washed ashore.

chapters.title: What the Tide Keeps
chapters.summary: At the mortuary, Felix notes the clothes are genuine, worn, not costumes — someone owned Maren's life. The coroner, an old ally, warns him off. POV: Felix. Beat: dread sharpening into obsession.

chapters.title: Three Accidents, One Hand
chapters.summary: Felix revisits his three quiet cases and maps them against the old Voss investigation; all four deaths cluster around the Harrow Point development deal. POV: Felix. Beat: pattern recognition, the hunter waking.

chapters.title: The Archivist of Gull Row
chapters.summary: Chasing paper trails, Felix meets Odile Brandt, the town archive's reclusive keeper who flinches at Maren's name. He notices salt-bleached hands and a habit of watching the tide tables. POV: Felix. Beat: suspicion entwined with unexpected tenderness.

chapters.title: A Letter, Six Years Late
chapters.summary: Among his dead wife's effects, Felix finds a letter Maren mailed him the week she vanished — half a sentence, cut off mid-warning. POV: Felix, with the letter's voice interleaved. Beat: grief reopened; the case becomes personal penance.

chapters.title: The Man Who Buys Silence
chapters.summary: Developer Aldous Crane, now a philanthropist, hosts a charity night; Felix attends and watches Crane's fixer, Nils Ferrar, watch him back. POV: alternating Felix and Ferrar. Beat: menace in good tailoring.

chapters.title: Drowned Twice
chapters.summary: Felix digs up the original inquest: Maren's body was never found, only her coat on the rocks — yet a death certificate exists, signed by a doctor since deceased. POV: Felix. Beat: the machinery of official lies exposed tooth by tooth.

chapters.title: Someone Is Still Writing Her
chapters.summary: A second body appears, staged again in Maren's clothing, proving the killer knows she lived — and is killing to keep her dead on paper. POV: Ferrar, executing the staging with chilling professionalism. Beat: villain POV reveals stakes and method.

chapters.title: The Bookshop Burns Slowly
chapters.summary: An 'electrical fault' guts half of Felix's shop; among the ashes he finds kerosene and a tide chart marked at the quarry. POV: Felix. Beat: loss transmuted into fury.

chapters.title: Odile's Locked Room
chapters.summary: Felix confronts Odile with the tide chart; she denies everything but her archive contains Maren's handwriting, fresh, cataloguing Crane's land purchases under false names. POV: Odile. Beat: terror of a woman guarding a secret with her life.

chapters.title: The Quarry at Low Water
chapters.summary: Felix dives the flooded quarry and finds a waterproof case: ledgers, photographs, and a confession draft in Maren's hand — evidence she hid before vanishing. POV: Felix. Beat: triumph curdling into danger as a boat engine sounds above.

chapters.title: Witness, Deceased
chapters.summary: Ferrar corners Felix, offers money and then threats; Felix realizes Ferrar has known where Maren is for years and was paid to forget — until now. POV: Felix and Ferrar. Beat: corruption shown as a bargain everyone keeps making.

chapters.title: The Doctor's Widow
chapters.summary: The inquest doctor's widow reveals Maren didn't die — she paid the doctor to certify a corpse, trading her identity for survival after witnessing Crane's first murder. POV: Felix. Beat: the price of survival made explicit and pitiable.

chapters.title: Crane's Cathedral
chapters.summary: At the dedication of Crane's waterfront memorial — built where the bodies were found — Felix publicly needles him and watches the mask slip for one unguarded second. POV: Felix. Beat: power's vanity as the crack in its armor.

chapters.title: Betrayal in the Stacks
chapters.summary: Ferrar raids the archive; Odile burns what she can and flees to Felix, confessing she is Maren Voss — alive, hidden, and done running. POV: Odile/Maren. Beat: the book's central reveal, delivered as surrender and relief at once.

chapters.title: Why She Let Him Drown
chapters.summary: Maren tells the whole story: the murder she witnessed, the death she bought, the years watching Felix solve other people's dead while she stayed silent. POV: Maren. Beat: guilt, anger, and the question of whether survival was worth its cost.

chapters.title: The Trap at Gull Row
chapters.summary: They bait Ferrar with the recovered ledgers; the exchange goes wrong, Odile is taken, and Felix lets himself be captured to follow. POV: Felix. Beat: plan collapsing into sacrifice.

chapters.title: High Water
chapters.summary: In the quarry pump-house, Crane arrives to erase the last loose ends personally; Felix turns the tables using the tide schedule — flooding the chamber where Crane kept his own blackmail archive. POV: Felix. Beat: climax; the corrupt drowned by their own secrets.

chapters.title: What the Tide Gives Up
chapters.summary: As waters recede, the quarry yields Crane's records and the truth of every staged death; Ferrar, abandoned, trades testimony for leniency. POV: Felix. Beat: vindication that tastes like ash.

chapters.title: The Unquiet Letter
chapters.summary: Maren completes the unfinished letter aloud, choosing to testify under her real name rather than stay buried; Felix stands beside her as the state finally reopens the case. POV: Maren. Beat: reclaiming a stolen life at the cost of safety.

chapters.title: Open at Dawn
chapters.summary: Weeks later, the bookshop reopens with new shelves and Odile's name on the lease beside his; the sea is quiet, and for once Felix doesn't check the tide tables. POV: Felix. Beat: hard-won peace, memory honored rather than feared.
